greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Grace and peace be with you all as we gather in prayer.
penitential:
Lord Jesus, you call us to pray without growing weary. Lord, have mercy.
Christ Jesus, you are the justice and the light of our souls. Christ, have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you hold our loved ones in your eternal peace. Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: Blessed the man who fears the Lord.
homily:
We begin today with something very small, very ordinary, and very easy to overlook: a pair of shoes left near the front door. Think of them. They are scuffed at the toes, slightly worn at the heels, shaped by the exact footprint of someone who walked through the rooms of a home just yesterday. A pair of shoes left by the door is a quiet promise. It tells anyone walking past that the person who wore them is only out for a moment, that they will be back, that life is moving forward in its usual, rhythmic way. We look at those shoes and we assume there will be an evening conversation, a shared meal, another morning to wake up and see the world together. There is a deep, quiet comfort in the ordinary things we leave behind.

I want you to hold onto this image: the shoes by the door. It is the image of a journey interrupted, but it is also the image of a presence that lingers. It is the image of Benjamin Vo. Think of his brilliant, searching mind, always looking toward the horizon, always curious about how things worked—whether he was exploring the architecture of the cloud, talking about aviation, or giggling when he mentioned his dream of starting ‘con chim airlines.’ He was a boy who moved through the world with a bright, open spirit, leaving his quiet footprint everywhere he went. He was a boy who loved the journey, loved the wide world, and loved the family that walked beside him.

Let us tell the truth of the heart before we look for the comfort. Alan, Thao, Ryan, and all of you who hold the memory of Benjamin as a sacred trust: it has been five months since he went home to God. We know the reality of your quiet house. We know the moments when the silence becomes a weight, when the habits of a lifetime—the quick laugh, the bright smile with the braces, the sound of a familiar voice down the hallway—are suddenly met with an empty space. You are grieving. You are carrying a cross that is heavy, real, and unrelenting. You are allowed to be tired. You are allowed to feel the sudden ache when a memory ambushes you in the middle of an ordinary Tuesday. Do not pretend the weight is lighter than it is. Do not rush to be strong for others if your heart is currently breaking. Your honesty before God is the most authentic prayer you can offer.

And let us gently lift one particular stone from your hearts today—a stone that grief often slips into our pockets without us noticing. Sometimes, when a family suffers an unimaginable loss, the mind begins to circle back, whispering quiet, unfair questions. Did we miss a sign? Could we have done something more? Could we have watched closer? Let us lay that burden down right here at the altar. You missed nothing. You loved Benjamin with a completeness that filled his fifteen years with the richness of a lifetime—traveling the globe together from the streets of Asia to the sacred places of Europe, sharing quiet stories, and walking side by side as a family of four. You were the exact parents and the exact brother that Benjamin needed. Let that heavy stone fall; you are absolved, and you are held. You did not fail him in any way. You were the light in his life, just as he was the light in yours. Some things in this life are simply beyond our control, and God does not hold you responsible for the mysteries of the cross. You are held in His mercy, not judged by your sorrow. You are not to blame for the randomness of the world’s suffering. You are simply loved.

Now, let the Gospel break into that quiet room. Jesus tells his disciples a parable about a persistent widow and an unjust judge, teaching them 'the necessity for them to pray always without becoming weary.' It is a strange parable at first glance. It compares God not to the dishonest judge, but to the one who listens because the cry is constant, because the heart will not let go. Prayer, Jesus tells us, is not about changing God's mind; it is about keeping our hearts turned toward the light until the dawn breaks. Think of how Benjamin lived with that kind of persistent, open-hearted generosity. Think of that remarkable moment when he, at just fifteen years old and completely unprompted, told his parents he was willing to give up his entire piggy bank to help his uncle William, who was suffering. He didn't need to break it open—it was never broken, and the help wasn't needed because of insurance—but the offer itself revealed the magnificent generosity of his soul. He was a boy whose heart was already sized for eternity. He was a boy who knew that the true wealth of life is not what we keep, but what we are willing to offer for the sake of those we love.

Consider the first reading from the Third Letter of John: 'Beloved, you are faithful in all you do for the brothers and sisters, especially for strangers; they have testified to your love before the Church. Please help them in a way worthy of God to continue their journey.' John is writing to encourage a community that is walking a difficult road, reminding them that every act of love, every kindness offered in secret, becomes part of the enduring truth of God's kingdom. Benjamin walked in that truth. Think of the way he smiled when he shared a meal, the way he laughed when he tried something silly like eating spicy Pad Thai in Bangkok with his dad and tearing up while giggling at the same time. He found joy in the small, unexpected moments of life. He was a risk-taker in joy, a boy who embraced the adventure of being alive. That love is still flowing. It flows in the clean water of the well dedicated in his name in Cà Mau, bringing life to those in need. It flows in the quiet memories shared by everyone who knew his gentle spirit. His love did not stop when he crossed the threshold; it continues to work in the world, quietly and persistently.

Ryan, you are a brother who carries a unique, holy weight. You know the memories better than anyone. You know the shared laughter, the boba tea outings, the quiet moments of being brothers. You are not just a brother who remains; you are a brother who continues the story. When you look at the sky, when you think of the future, remember that you are not doing it alone. You are carrying the legacy of his joy. You are a witness to the world that love is not a finite resource. It is a well that never runs dry. Keep being the boy who reaches out. Keep being the one who values the small, human moments. You are a vital part of this family of four, and your life is a testament to the fact that love is the most durable thing we possess. Your brother's love is not gone; it is woven into the very fabric of who you are becoming. He is cheering for you, and he is walking with you in the quiet places of your heart.

We hear in the Psalm today: 'Blessed the man who fears the Lord, who greatly delights in his commands... Light shines through the darkness for the upright; he is gracious and merciful and just.' This is the turn of the heart. The light does not eliminate the darkness; it shines right through it. It pierces the shadow and shows us that we are never alone. Benjamin is now resting in that uncreated light. He is dwelling in the land of the living, fully alive, fully healed, and fully embraced by the Father. He is not a memory tucked away in a photo album; he is a living soul in the Banquet of Heaven, standing alongside kindred spirits like Saint Carlo Acutis, watching over you with a love that has been purified and perfected. Think of the dream Alan had, where Ben and his dad stood outside room 419, and Ben said with that earnest voice, 'Ba ơi, test nào con cũng qua hết... Không sao đâu, con sẽ dõi theo ba mẹ.' That dream was a whisper from heaven. It was the assurance that he has passed every test, that he is whole, and that he is watching over you with a smile.

There is a peace that comes from knowing that we are held. It is not a peace that takes away the pain overnight, but it is a peace that keeps us from being destroyed by it. It is the peace of knowing that Benjamin is waiting. He is waiting in the light, waiting in the place where there is no more struggling, only the clear, bright presence of God. He is waiting for you with that same sweet, gentle smile that you remember so vividly. That smile is the promise that the reunion is certain. He is a light in the world, and he is shining for you. He is home. And because he is home, you are never truly lost.

To everyone tuning in from afar—especially other children who are carrying heavy crosses of suffering, and every family whose home feels too quiet today—hear this: you are seen by God. You are not forgotten. The Lord draws closest to the brokenhearted, and His mercy is broad enough to hold every single one of our tears.

So, what do you carry out the door today? Not a summary, not a heavy burden, but one small, doable thing: when the grief rises and the house feels too quiet, pause. Close your eyes. Breathe in. Imagine the Lord reaching into the silence, and imagine Benjamin standing beside you, smiling that bright, easy grin, looking out toward an endless horizon. Let yourself be gathered into the peace of Christ. Walk out knowing that you are loved, that you are not to blame, and that the one who went before you is waiting at the door of eternity. You are not a broken family. You are a family of four, and you are being held in the palm of God's hand. Keep your heart open to that truth. Keep your eyes on the light. And remember that he is watching over you, always, with love that knows no end. Amen.
petitions: For Benjamin, and for all who have died, that they may rest forever in the light and peace of Christ, we pray to the Lord.
For all who grieve and carry heavy crosses, especially Alan, Thao, Ryan, and their family, that God may console them with His presence and fill them with enduring hope, we pray to the Lord.
communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, make His face shine upon you and be gracious to you, and give you His peace, now and forever. Amen.
standing_petitions: For a boy named Ben and all who have died, that they rest in the light of Christ.
For all who grieve, that God console them and give them hope.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
Beloved, you are faithful in all you do for the brothers and sisters,
especially for strangers;
they have testified to your love before the Church.
Please help them in a way worthy of God to continue their journey.
For they have set out for the sake of the Name
and are accepting nothing from the pagans.
Therefore, we ought to support such persons,
so that we may be co-workers in the truth.

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. Blessed the man who fears the Lord.
or:
R. Alleluia.
Blessed the man who fears the LORD,
who greatly delights in his commands.
His posterity shall be mighty upon the earth;
the upright generation shall be blessed.
R. Blessed the man who fears the Lord.
or:
R. Alleluia.
Wealth and riches shall be in his house;
his generosity shall endure forever.
Light shines through the darkness for the upright;
he is gracious and merciful and just.
R. Blessed the man who fears the Lord.
or:
R. Alleluia.
Well for the man who is gracious and lends,
who conducts his affairs with justice;
He shall never be moved;
the just one shall be in everlasting remembrance.
R. Blessed the man who fears the Lord.
or:
R. Alleluia.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
Jesus told his disciples a parable
about the necessity for them to pray always without becoming weary. 
He said, “There was a judge in a certain town
who neither feared God nor respected any human being. 
And a widow in that town used to come to him and say,
‘Render a just decision for me against my adversary.’
For a long time the judge was unwilling, but eventually he thought,
‘While it is true that I neither fear God nor respect any human being, 
because this widow keeps bothering me
I shall deliver a just decision for her
lest she finally come and strike me.’” 
The Lord said, “Pay attention to what the dishonest judge says. 
Will not God then secure the rights of his chosen ones
who call out to him day and night? 
Will he be slow to answer them? 
I tell you, he will see to it that justice is done for them speedily. 
But when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on earth?”

pet_prayers.text: Nha Trang, ngày 31/10/2026, anh Minh suy nghĩ về Ben rất nhiều. Nhớ và thương em!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - mom and I have been missing you a lot.   Saw you a few times in my dreams last few weeks! Come and say hi daily okay?
Thinking of you buddy! Stop by to say hello whenever you can okay? Love you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - Been dreaming about you a lot. Hope you're having fun up in heaven. Please look after our family. Remember to come say hi daily. We miss you so much!

Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever
